sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan saṃśayaṃ pṛṣṭas taṃ me vyākhyātum arhasi cāturvarṇyasya yo dharmaḥ sve sve varṇe guṇāvahaḥ
english: Umā said: O Lord, having been asked of my doubt, you should explain it to me — the dharma proper to the four orders, that which brings merit to each in its own order.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇe kīdṛśo dharmaḥ kṣatriye kīdṛśo bhavet vaiśye kiṃlakṣaṇo dharmaḥ śūdre kiṃlakṣaṇo bhavet
english: What kind of dharma belongs to the brāhmaṇa, what kind to the kṣatriya? What is the mark of dharma for the vaiśya, and what its mark for the śūdra?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca nyāyatas te mahābhāge saṃśayaḥ samudīritaḥ bhūmidevā mahābhāgāḥ sadā loke dvijātayaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: Justly, O greatly blessed one, has your doubt been raised. The twice-born in this world are ever the highly honored gods upon earth.

sanskrit: upavāsaḥ sadā dharmo brāhmaṇasya na saṃśayaḥ sa hi dharmārtham utpanno brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: Fasting is ever the dharma of the brāhmaṇa — of this there is no doubt; for he is born for the sake of dharma and is fit to attain unto Brahman.

sanskrit: tasya dharmakriyā devi vratacaryā ca nyāyataḥ tathopanayanaṃ caiva dvijāyaivopapadyate
english: For him, O goddess, the performance of dharmic rites, the observance of vows according to rule, and likewise the sacred initiation — these befit the twice-born alone.

sanskrit: gurudaivatapūjārthaṃ svādhyāyābhyasanātmakaḥ dehibhir dharmaparamaiś cartavyo dharmasaṃbhavaḥ
english: For the honoring of teacher and deity, consisting in the practice of self-study — this wellspring of dharma must be observed by embodied beings devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan saṃśayo me 'tra taṃ me vyākhyātum arhasi cāturvarṇyasya dharmaṃ hi naipuṇyena prakīrtaya
english: Umā said: O Lord, herein lies my doubt; you should explain it to me. Proclaim with precision the dharma of the four orders.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca rahasyaśravaṇaṃ dharmo vedavrataniṣevaṇam vratacaryāparo dharmo gurupādaprasādanam
english: Maheśvara said: The hearing of the secret teachings is dharma, and the keeping of the Vedic vows; devotion to the observance of vows is dharma, and the gracious service of the teacher's feet.

sanskrit: bhaikṣacaryāparo dharmo dharmo nityopavāsitā nityasvādhyāyitā dharmo brahmacaryāśramas tathā
english: Devotion to the gathering of alms is dharma; constant fasting is dharma; constant self-study is dharma, and likewise the stage of chaste studentship.

sanskrit: guruṇā tv abhyanujñātaḥ samāvarteta vai dvijaḥ vindetānantaraṃ bhāryām anurūpāṃ yathāvidhi
english: And when permitted by his teacher, the twice-born should return home; thereafter he should take a fitting wife according to the rule.

sanskrit: śūdrānnavarjanaṃ dharmas tathā satpathasevanam dharmo nityopavāsitvaṃ brahmacaryaṃ tathaiva ca
english: The shunning of a śūdra's food is dharma, and the following of the good path; constant fasting is dharma, and likewise continence.

sanskrit: āhitāgnir adhīyāno juhvānaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ vighasāśī yatāhāro gṛhasthaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ
english: Having kindled the sacred fires, studying, offering oblation, with senses restrained, eating the remnants of sacrifice, moderate in food, truthful of speech and pure — such is the householder.

sanskrit: atithivratatā dharmo dharmas tretāgnidhāraṇam iṣṭīś ca paśubandhāṃś ca vidhipūrvaṃ samācaret
english: Devotion to the vow of hospitality is dharma, and the maintaining of the three fires is dharma; the iṣṭi-rites and the animal sacrifices he should perform in due order.

sanskrit: yajñaś ca paramo dharmas tathāhiṃsā ca dehiṣu apūrvabhojanaṃ dharmo vighasāśitvam eva ca
english: Sacrifice is the highest dharma, and likewise non-injury toward embodied beings; not to eat before others is dharma, and the eating of the sacrificial remnants.

sanskrit: bhukte parijane paścād bhojanaṃ dharma ucyate brāhmaṇasya gṛhasthasya śrotriyasya viśeṣataḥ
english: To eat afterward, once the household has eaten, is declared to be dharma — especially for the brāhmaṇa householder learned in the Veda.

sanskrit: daṃpatyoḥ samaśīlatvaṃ dharmaś ca gṛhamedhinām gṛhyāṇāṃ caiva devānāṃ nityaṃ puṣpabalikriyā
english: Harmony of character between husband and wife is the dharma of householders, and the constant offering of flowers and oblations to the household deities.

sanskrit: nityopalepanaṃ dharmas tathā nityopavāsitā susaṃmṛṣṭopalipte ca sājyadhūmodgame gṛhe
english: Daily anointing of the dwelling is dharma, and likewise constant fasting — in a house well-swept and freshly smeared, where the smoke of ghee rises up.

sanskrit: eṣa dvijajane dharmo gārhasthyo lokadhāraṇaḥ dvijātīnāṃ satāṃ nityaṃ sadaivaiṣa pravartate
english: This is the householder's dharma among the twice-born, the sustainer of the world; among the good twice-born it ever holds sway, always.

sanskrit: yas tu kṣatragato devi tvayā dharma udīritaḥ tam ahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi taṃ me śṛṇu samāhitā
english: But that dharma pertaining to the kṣatriya, which you have raised, O goddess — that I shall declare to you; hear it from me with attentive mind.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya smṛto dharmaḥ prajāpālanam āditaḥ nirdiṣṭaphalabhoktā hi rājā dharmeṇa yujyate
english: The dharma of the kṣatriya is held to be, first of all, the protection of the people; for the king who enjoys his appointed reward is thereby joined with dharma.

sanskrit: prajāḥ pālayate yo hi dharmeṇa manujādhipaḥ tasya dharmārjitā lokāḥ prajāpālanasaṃcitāḥ
english: The lord of men who protects his people in accordance with dharma — for him there are worlds won by dharma, accumulated through the protection of his people.

sanskrit: tatra rājñaḥ paro dharmo damaḥ svādhyāya eva ca agnihotraparispando dānādhyayanam eva ca
english: Therein the king's foremost dharma is self-restraint and self-study, the busy tending of the sacred fire, and likewise giving and learning.

sanskrit: yajñopavītadhāraṇaṃ yajño dharmakriyās tathā bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇaṃ dharmaḥ kṛte karmaṇy amoghatā
english: The wearing of the sacred thread, sacrifice, and the performance of dharmic rites; the maintenance of his dependents is dharma, and unfailingness when a deed is to be done.

sanskrit: samyag daṇḍe sthitir dharmo dharmo vedakratukriyāḥ vyavahārasthitir dharmaḥ satyavākyaratis tathā
english: Standing firm in just punishment is dharma; the performance of Vedic sacrifices is dharma; abiding by lawful judgment is dharma, and likewise delight in truthful speech.

sanskrit: ārtahastaprado rājā pretya ceha mahīyate gobrāhmaṇārthe vikrāntaḥ saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ gataḥ aśvamedhajitāṃl lokān prāpnoti tridivālaye
english: The king who lends a hand to the distressed is exalted both here and hereafter; and one who, valiant for the sake of cattle and brāhmaṇas, meets his death in battle, attains the worlds won by the horse-sacrifice, in the abode of the third heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśyasya satataṃ dharmaḥ pāśupālyaṃ kṛṣis tathā agnihotraparispando dānādhyayanam eva ca
english: The constant dharma of the vaiśya is the tending of cattle and tillage, the busy tending of the sacred fire, and likewise giving and learning.

sanskrit: vāṇijyaṃ satpathasthānam ātithyaṃ praśamo damaḥ viprāṇāṃ svāgataṃ tyāgo vaiśyadharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Trade conducted upon the honest path, hospitality, tranquility, self-restraint, the welcoming of brāhmaṇas, and liberality — this is the eternal dharma of the vaiśya.

sanskrit: tilān gandhān rasāṃś caiva na vikrīṇīta vai kva cit vaṇikpatham upāsīno vaiśyaḥ satpatham āśritaḥ
english: Sesame, perfumes, and liquids he should never sell anywhere; following the merchant's calling, the vaiśya keeps to the honest path.

sanskrit: sarvātithyaṃ trivargasya yathāśakti yathārhataḥ śūdradharmaḥ paro nityaṃ śuśrūṣā ca dvijātiṣu
english: Full hospitality to the three orders, according to his means and as is fitting — and the highest constant dharma of the śūdra is service rendered to the twice-born.

sanskrit: sa śūdraḥ saṃśitatapāḥ satyasaṃdho jitendriyaḥ śuśrūṣann atithiṃ prāptaṃ tapaḥ saṃcinute mahat
english: That śūdra, steadfast in austerity, true to his word, with senses conquered, who serves the guest that has arrived, accumulates great austerity.

sanskrit: tyaktahiṃsaḥ śubhācāro devatādvijapūjakaḥ śūdro dharmaphalair iṣṭaiḥ saṃprayujyeta buddhimān
english: Having abandoned violence, of pure conduct, a worshipper of the deities and the twice-born — such a wise śūdra is united with the cherished fruits of dharma.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ cāturvarṇyasya śobhane ekaikasyeha subhage kim anyac chrotum icchasi
english: All this has been told to you, O lovely one, concerning each of the four orders here. What else, O blessed one, do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: umovāca uktās tvayā pṛthagdharmāś cāturvarṇyahitāḥ śubhāḥ sarvavyāpī tu yo dharmo bhagavaṃs taṃ bravīhi me
english: Umā said: You have told the separate, auspicious dharmas befitting the four orders. But that dharma which is all-pervading, O Lord — that one tell me.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca brāhmaṇā lokasāreṇa sṛṣṭā dhātrā guṇārthinā lokāṃs tārayituṃ kṛtsnān martyeṣu kṣitidevatāḥ
english: Maheśvara said: The brāhmaṇas were created by the Maker, seeking virtue, out of the very essence of the world, to ferry all the worlds across — gods upon earth among mortals.

sanskrit: teṣām imaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmakarmaphalodayam brāhmaṇeṣu hi yo dharmaḥ sa dharmaḥ paramo mataḥ
english: Of them I shall declare this arising of the fruit of dharmic deeds; for the dharma that is among the brāhmaṇas is held to be the supreme dharma.

sanskrit: ime tu lokadharmārthaṃ trayaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā pṛthivyāḥ sarjane nityaṃ sṛṣṭās tān api me śṛṇu
english: But these three were created by the Self-Born for the sake of the world's dharma, ever created for the bringing forth of the earth; hear of them too from me.

sanskrit: vedoktaḥ paramo dharmaḥ smṛtiśāstragato 'paraḥ śiṣṭācīrṇaḥ paraḥ proktas trayo dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: The supreme dharma is that declared in the Veda; another is that found in the smṛti-treatises; another, it is said, is that practiced by the cultured — these three are the eternal dharmas.

sanskrit: traividyo brāhmaṇo vidvān na cādhyayanajīvanaḥ trikarmā triparikrānto maitra eṣa smṛto dvijaḥ
english: A brāhmaṇa learned in the three Vedas, yet not living merely by recitation, performing the three duties, having gone through the three stages, friendly toward all — such a one is held to be a true twice-born.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ imāni tu karmāṇi provāca bhuvaneśvaraḥ vṛttyarthaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vai śṛṇu tāni samāhitā
english: These six duties the Lord of the world declared for the livelihood of the brāhmaṇas; hear them, O attentive one.

sanskrit: yajanaṃ yājanaṃ caiva tathā dānapratigrahau adhyāpanam adhītaṃ ca ṣaṭkarmā dharmabhāg dvijaḥ
english: Sacrificing and officiating at sacrifice, likewise giving and receiving gifts, teaching and being taught — the twice-born of the six duties is a sharer in dharma.

sanskrit: nityasvādhyāyatā dharmo dharmo yajñaḥ sanātanaḥ dānaṃ praśasyate cāsya yathāśakti yathāvidhi
english: Constant self-study is dharma; sacrifice is the eternal dharma; and giving, according to his means and according to rule, is praised in him.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu paramo dharmaḥ pravṛttaḥ satsu nityaśaḥ gṛhasthatā viśuddhānāṃ dharmasya nicayo mahān
english: But this is the supreme dharma, ever practiced among the good: the householder's life of the wholly pure is a great treasury of dharma.

sanskrit: pañcayajñaviśuddhātmā satyavāg anasūyakaḥ dātā brāhmaṇasatkartā susaṃmṛṣṭaniveśanaḥ
english: His self purified by the five sacrifices, truthful of speech, free of malice, a giver, an honorer of brāhmaṇas, his dwelling well-swept —

sanskrit: amānī ca sadājihmaḥ snigdhavāṇīpradas tathā atithyabhyāgataratiḥ śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ
english: free of pride and ever upright, speaking words made gentle, delighting in the guest who has come, making his meal of the remnants of food —

sanskrit: pādyam arghyaṃ yathānyāyam āsanaṃ śayanaṃ tathā dīpaṃ pratiśrayaṃ cāpi yo dadāti sa dhārmikaḥ
english: who offers, as is right, water for the feet, the welcome-offering, a seat, a bed, a lamp, and shelter too — he is the righteous one.

sanskrit: prātar utthāya cācamya bhojanenopamantrya ca satkṛtyānuvrajed yaś ca tasya dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Rising at dawn and sipping water for purification, inviting the guest with food, and who, having honored him, walks after him a way in farewell — his is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: sarvātithyaṃ trivargasya yathāśakti divāniśam śūdradharmaḥ samākhyātas trivarṇaparicāraṇam
english: Full hospitality to the three orders, according to means, by day and night — the dharma of the śūdra has been declared to be service to the three orders.

sanskrit: pravṛttilakṣaṇo dharmo gṛhastheṣu vidhīyate tam ahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvabhūtahitaṃ śubham
english: The dharma marked by active engagement is ordained among householders; that one I shall proclaim — auspicious and for the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: dātavyam asakṛc chaktyā yaṣṭavyam asakṛt tathā puṣṭikarmavidhānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: Gifts should be given again and again, according to one's power, and likewise sacrifice should be offered again and again; and the rites that bring increase should be performed by one who desires prosperity.

sanskrit: dharmeṇārthaḥ samāhāryo dharmalabdhaṃ tridhā dhanam kartavyaṃ dharmaparamaṃ mānavena prayatnataḥ
english: Wealth should be gathered by dharma; the riches gained through dharma are threefold; a man should make dharma supreme with diligent effort.

sanskrit: ekenāṃśena dharmārthaś cartavyo bhūtim icchatā ekenāṃśena kāmārtha ekam aṃśaṃ vivardhayet
english: With one portion the aim of dharma should be served by one who desires prosperity; with one portion the aim of pleasure; and one portion he should make to grow.

sanskrit: nivṛttilakṣaṇas tv anyo dharmo mokṣa iti smṛtaḥ tasya vṛttiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu me devi tattvataḥ
english: But another dharma, marked by withdrawal, is remembered as liberation; its way of life I shall declare — hear it from me, O goddess, in its truth.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtadayā dharmo na caikagrāmavāsitā āśāpāśavimokṣaś ca śasyate mokṣakāṅkṣiṇām
english: Compassion for all beings is dharma, and not dwelling in a single village; and release from the bonds of craving is praised for those who long for liberation.

sanskrit: na kuṇḍyāṃ nodake saṅgo na vāsasi na cāsane na tridaṇḍe na śayane nāgnau na śaraṇālaye
english: No attachment to a water-pot, nor to water, nor to clothing, nor to a seat, nor to the triple staff, nor to a bed, nor to fire, nor to a place of shelter.

sanskrit: adhyātmagatacitto yas tanmanās tatparāyaṇaḥ yukto yogaṃ prati sadā pratisaṃkhyānam eva ca
english: He whose mind is fixed on the Supreme Self, whose thought is on That, devoted to That, ever intent upon yoga and likewise upon discriminating reflection —

sanskrit: vṛkṣamūlaśayo nityaṃ śūnyāgāraniveśanaḥ nadīpulinaśāyī ca nadītīraratiś ca yaḥ
english: sleeping ever at the root of a tree, dwelling in an empty house, lying upon the sandbanks of a river, and delighting on a river's bank —

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvasaṅgeṣu snehabandheṣu ca dvijaḥ ātmany evātmano bhāvaṃ samāsajyāṭati dvijaḥ
english: the twice-born freed from all attachments and from the bonds of affection — fixing the being of the self in the Self alone, the twice-born wanders.

sanskrit: sthāṇubhūto nirāhāro mokṣadṛṣṭena karmaṇā parivrajati yo yuktas tasya dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Become motionless as a post, fasting, by deeds directed toward liberation — he who, disciplined, goes forth as a wandering mendicant, his is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: na caikatra cirāsakto na caikagrāmagocaraḥ yukto hy aṭati nirmukto na caikapulineśayaḥ
english: Not long attached in any one place, nor ranging within a single village, disciplined and released he wanders, not sleeping always on one sandbank.

sanskrit: eṣa mokṣavidāṃ dharmo vedoktaḥ satpathaḥ satām yo mārgam anuyātīmaṃ padaṃ tasya na vidyate
english: This is the dharma of those who know liberation, the good path of the good, declared in the Veda; for one who follows this road, no further state of rebirth exists.

sanskrit: caturvidhā bhikṣavas te kuṭīcarakṛtodakaḥ haṃsaḥ paramahaṃsaś ca yo yaḥ paścāt sa uttamaḥ
english: The mendicants are of four kinds: the kuṭīcara, the kṛtodaka, the haṃsa, and the paramahaṃsa; and whichever comes later, that one is the higher.

sanskrit: ataḥ parataraṃ nāsti nādharaṃ na tiro 'grataḥ aduḥkham asukhaṃ saumyam ajarāmaram avyayam
english: Beyond this there is nothing higher, nothing lower, nothing aside or in front — that which is without sorrow, without pleasure, gentle, free of age, deathless, and imperishable.

sanskrit: umovāca gārhasthyo mokṣadharmaś ca sajjanācaritas tvayā bhāṣito martyalokasya mārgaḥ śreyaskaro mahān
english: Umā said: The dharma of the householder and the dharma of liberation, practiced by the good, you have set forth — the great and beneficial road for the world of mortals.

sanskrit: ṛṣidharmaṃ tu dharmajña śrotum icchāmy anuttamam spṛhā bhavati me nityaṃ tapovananivāsiṣu
english: But the dharma of the seers, O knower of dharma, I wish to hear — that unsurpassed dharma; for I have a constant longing toward those who dwell in the groves of austerity.

sanskrit: ājyadhūmodbhavo gandho ruṇaddhīva tapovanam taṃ dṛṣṭvā me manaḥ prītaṃ maheśvara sadā bhavet
english: The fragrance arising from the smoke of ghee seems to fill the whole grove of austerity; beholding it, my mind, O Maheśvara, would ever be glad.

sanskrit: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ deva munidharmakṛtaṃ vibho sarvadharmārthatattvajña devadeva vadasva me nikhilena mayā pṛṣṭaṃ mahādeva yathātatham
english: This doubt of mine concerning the dharma of the sages, O God, O mighty one, O knower of the truth of all dharma and its aims, O God of gods, tell me in full — O Mahādeva, as I have asked, just as it is.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca hanta te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi munidharmam anuttamam yaṃ kṛtvā munayo yānti siddhiṃ svatapasā śubhe
english: Maheśvara said: Behold, I shall declare to you the unsurpassed dharma of the sages, by following which the sages attain perfection through their own austerity, O lovely one.

sanskrit: phenapānām ṛṣīṇāṃ yo dharmo dharmavidāṃ sadā taṃ me śṛṇu mahābhāge dharmajñe dharmam āditaḥ
english: The dharma that belongs ever to the foam-drinking seers, the knowers of dharma — hear it from me, O greatly blessed one, O knower of dharma, that dharma from the beginning.

sanskrit: uñchanti satataṃ tasmin brāhmaṃ phenotkaraṃ śubham amṛtaṃ brahmaṇā pītaṃ madhuraṃ prasṛtaṃ divi
english: Therein they ever glean the holy, auspicious mass of foam — that sweet nectar drunk by Brahmā, spread abroad in heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa teṣāṃ viśuddhānāṃ phenapānāṃ tapodhane dharmacaryākṛto mārgo vālakhilyagaṇe śṛṇu
english: This is the road wrought by the practice of dharma for those wholly pure foam-drinkers, O you whose wealth is austerity; now hear of the host of the Vālakhilyas.

sanskrit: vālakhilyās tapaḥsiddhā munayaḥ sūryamaṇḍale uñcham uñchanti dharmajñāḥ śākunīṃ vṛttim āsthitāḥ
english: The Vālakhilyas, sages perfected in austerity, within the orb of the sun — knowers of dharma, they glean the gleanings, abiding by the way of life of the birds.

sanskrit: mṛganirmokavasanāś cīravalkalavāsasaḥ nirdvaṃdvāḥ satpathaṃ prāptā vālakhilyās tapodhanāḥ
english: Clothed in deerskins, garbed in rags and bark, beyond the pairs of opposites, having reached the good path — such are the Vālakhilyas, whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhaparvamātrās te sveṣv aṅgeṣu vyavasthitāḥ tapaścaraṇam īhante teṣāṃ dharmaphalaṃ mahat
english: No larger than a thumb-joint, settled firmly within their own bodies, they strive at the practice of austerity; great is the fruit of their dharma.

sanskrit: te suraiḥ samatāṃ yānti surakāryārthasiddhaye dyotayanto diśaḥ sarvās tapasā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ
english: They attain equality with the gods, for the accomplishing of the gods' purposes, illumining all the quarters, their sins burned away by austerity.

sanskrit: ye tv anye śuddhamanaso dayādharmaparāyaṇāḥ santaś cakracarāḥ puṇyāḥ somalokacarāś ca ye
english: And those others, pure of mind, devoted to compassion and dharma, the good who move in companies, the holy ones who range the world of Soma —

sanskrit: pitṛlokasamīpasthās ta uñchanti yathāvidhi saṃprakṣālāśmakuṭṭāś ca dantolūkhalinas tathā
english: dwelling near the world of the fathers, they glean according to rule — the saṃprakṣālas and the aśmakuṭṭas, and likewise the dantolūkhalins.

sanskrit: somapānāṃ ca devānām ūṣmapāṇāṃ tathaiva ca uñchanti ye samīpasthāḥ svabhāvaniyatendriyāḥ
english: And those who, dwelling near the soma-drinking gods and likewise the vapor-drinking ones, glean their food, their senses restrained by their very nature —

sanskrit: teṣām agnipariṣyandaḥ pitṛdevārcanaṃ tathā yajñānāṃ cāpi pañcānāṃ yajanaṃ dharma ucyate
english: for them the tending of the sacred fire, the worship of the fathers and the gods, and likewise the offering of the five sacrifices is declared to be dharma.

sanskrit: eṣa cakracarair devi devalokacarair dvijaiḥ ṛṣidharmaḥ sadā cīrṇo yo 'nyas tam api me śṛṇu
english: This is the dharma of the seers, O goddess, ever practiced by the twice-born who move in companies and range the world of the gods; now hear from me that other dharma as well.

sanskrit: sarveṣv evarṣidharmeṣu jeya ātmā jitendriyaḥ kāmakrodhau tataḥ paścāj jetavyāv iti me matiḥ
english: In all the dharmas of the seers, the self is first to be conquered, the senses subdued; and thereafter desire and anger are to be conquered — such is my conviction.
